transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus target function, adapting the inherent `[T]` receiver to explicit `slice: &mut [T]` and `other: &mut [T]` parameters and attaching the generated equal-length precondition and two-slice final-frame postcondition.

Kept the Rust 1.96 equal-length assertion in the public target body as `assert!(slice.len() == other.len(), "destination and source slices have different lengths")`, lowered through a local helper whose precondition is discharged by the generated contract domain.

Preserved both target-body `as_mut_ptr` calls. The target-local helper contains the Rust raw slice cast and records a start-pointer relation plus unchanged frame, reusing the reviewed mutable slice pointer boundary shape rather than assuming the target postcondition.

Isolated only the unsafe raw-pointer operation `core::ptr::swap_nonoverlapping(dst, src, count)` in the target-local `rust_1_96_ptr_swap_nonoverlapping` boundary. The public target computes `count` from `slice.len()` after the two pointer calls and passes that value to the boundary, preserving the Rust 1.96 `self.len()` count.

Added a named source-backed final-frame bridge connecting the two pre-call slice views, the two `as_mut_ptr` start-pointer facts, and the `self.len()` count to the generated final relation `final(slice)@ == old(other)@` and `final(other)@ == old(slice)@`. This bridge is private to the harness; the public target is not `external_body`.
